sections.title: Above the fold
sections.guide: One headline: the practice area and the city, exactly as the ads say it. Under it, a free consultation in one line only when the firm truly offers one, and the phone as a tap-to-call button. Name the attorney responsible for the advertising.
sections.example: Divorce Attorney in Austin — free consultation. Call (512) 555-0100.

sections.title: Why this firm
sections.guide: Years in practice, the state bar admissions, the responsible attorney's name and the office address: several state bar rules require these on an advertising page. Real reviews with the reviewer's first name and the source; never a review the firm did not receive.
sections.example: 18 years in family law · Texas Bar · 100 Congress Ave, Austin

sections.title: What the consultation covers
sections.guide: A few plain sentences on what the first consultation covers and how it is billed: free, a flat fee, or 'flat fee from $X'. No promises about the outcome of a case.
sections.example: The first call is free. Most uncontested filings are a flat fee from $900.

sections.title: Request a call
sections.guide: Name, phone, the matter type, and a preferred time to call. Never ask for the facts of the case in the form; that conversation happens on the phone.
sections.example: We call back within one business day.

sections.title: Questions people ask
sections.guide: Four to six questions with one-paragraph answers: what the consultation costs, whether the firm handles cases like this one, how long a case like this typically takes, and the fee structure.
sections.example: What does a consultation cost? The first call is free; we discuss the case and what it may cost from there.

sections.title: Hours and where
sections.guide: Opening hours, the office address with a map link, the phone again.

sections.title: Footer
sections.guide: The firm's name, a Terms link, the Privacy notice link (required when the page has a form), and the firm's phone or e-mail.

form_rules: Never ask for the facts of the case in the form; that conversation happens on the phone.
Say when the firm calls back.
'specialist' only where the state certifies one.
faq: Do you handle cases like mine?
How long does a case like this take?
Is there parking at your office?
